question: Will Pete Hegseth still be Secretary of Defense (War) at the end of January 2027
quote: So I think he'll be gone by the end of January.
turn_text: So I think he'll be gone by the end of January. I think he's been overmatched by the job. I think directionally he had the right idea and a lot of regards. He was extremely optimistic about this venture, very out there in public, saying things it didn't necessarily prove out. It's just hard to fathom how the Pentagon wasn't aware of or didn't. You know, ultimately, this all goes to Trump. But our munitions would be in a low and dangerous place in some regards. So I think Trump will end up axing him. It'll be another echo of the Iraq War in 2006 when Don Rumsfeld, Secretary of Defense at the time, went right after the war. So I meant to do this in the first segment. I forgot. So we're going to double barrel this one, Noah, and go very meta with your friends at Audit the Editors. And we're going to predict whether Audit the Editors will still be around and like a going concern, like every single show for the duration. Or whether this is a flash in the pan and will be dropped sooner rather than later. What is the future of Audit the Editors?
host_quote: Pete Hexeth will be the Secretary of Defense slash war by the end of January. Yes or no? When the end of January comes, I should say. Yes or no?
resolution_criteria: Pete Hegseth holds the office of Secretary of Defense (also styled Secretary of War) on January 31, 2027. YES means he holds it; an announced but not yet effective departure still counts as holding. Resignation, dismissal or any other departure before that date means NO. Decided by the responsible body's own published record (an official announcement, filing, vote, opinion or data release). Resolves when the answer is a matter of record; the deadline is 2027-01-31.
